transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-18
- Start time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~64 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood Partner Ops); Lena Cho (Polaris Channel Lead), Marcus Avery (Polaris Head Strategic Alliances), Priya Nair (Polaris Sales Ops)

Auto-generated summary (quick):
- Workshop to align on co-sell plays, map pipeline, and agree next steps for 2 pilot opportunities. Discussed pricing/discount tiers, technical check (benchmarks for latency/cost), security requirements for enterprise pilots, and joint events pipeline. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Co-sell playbook alignment
- Deal mapping & prioritization criteria
- Pilot scoping and success metrics
- Technical gating: private deployment vs hosted, VPC, KMS, SOC2
- Joint marketing / event follow-ups

Action items (recap in meeting body)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour, hour and change. Um, I'll kick things off — Jordan from Redwood here, AE. With me is Priya, our SE, and Miguel from partner ops. Lena, Marcus, Priya, thanks for making time.

[00:18] Lena Cho: Thanks, Jordan. Appreciate it. We'll keep this pretty focused — want to get through pipeline and agree which deals we're prioritizing for a pilot.

[00:29] Jordan Blake: Perfect. High level agenda: 1) quick alignment on partner plays and discounting, 2) map the pipeline you shared, 3) decide two pilot deals and owners, 4) outline technical validation steps. Sound good?

[00:42] Marcus Avery: Yep, that works. Also want to make sure we talk about enablement — like joint decks and maybe an executive one-pager for customer execs.

[00:50] Miguel Santos: And timing — Polaris needs to get momentum before the January hiring freeze, so cadence is tight.

[01:02] Priya Raman: Quick note, on the SE side, we can run a two-week benchmark on our hosted API vs dedicated flow. But we should line up expected sequence lengths and concurrency so numbers are meaningful.

[01:18] Lena Cho: Good, we can share sample workloads. A couple of the deals are higher-concurrency for search and rerank, others are real-time assistants with low-latency SLOs.

[01:30] Jordan Blake: Great. Let's open the pipeline doc you dropped in the channel. I see six opportunities — let's go through each and categorize. Marcus, you want to walk us through top-line?

[01:43] Marcus Avery: Sure. Top one is NovaCare, healthcare payer — heavy PHI considerations. Two is Orion Retail, big e-comm personalization. Three is BlueCrest Fintech, want on-prem or VPC for compliance. Four is Aegis Logistics — typical real-time routing, low-latency. Five and six are smaller pilots — one internal proof for a product team and one pilot with an ISV.

[02:11] Jordan Blake: Okay, on NovaCare, sounds like security gating will be big. Do you have a SOC2 requirement or HIPAA BAAs?

[02:20] Lena Cho: Yes, they'd need a BAA and audit logs for data residency. Also KMS integration is a must — they want customer-managed keys.

[02:28] Priya Raman: Redwood Private supports KMS and on-premish flows — apologies, on-prem-ish, I mean Private VPC and HSM integrations, but there are some limits on the initial GA features. We can share the security matrix. Just FYI, some product names come out weird in notes, it's Redwood Privy in a draft deck, ignore that.

[02:50] Marcus Avery: Cool. BlueCrest also needs VPC and some offline model hosting, so might align with your Private flow.

[02:58] Jordan Blake: Right. For pricing and discounting — Miguel, do you want to summarize the co-sell discount tiers?

[03:04] Miguel Santos: Yeah — our standard partner uplift for mid-market pilots is 18% off list for first 3 months, sliding down after commit. For larger enterprise pilots we can do a reserved capacity commitment (Redwood Dedicated) with custom SLAs and discounting, which changes the economics. We should map the deal size to which path — hosted promo vs dedicated reserved.

[03:26] Lena Cho: For Polaris it's key we can offer a clear margin for our reps — if the discount is too thin they can't prioritize. Can we create a simple margin calculator they can plug numbers into?

[03:36] Jordan Blake: Yes — we'll add a one-sheet margin calculator. Miguel will own that.

[03:41] Priya Raman: On technical validation, my ask — for each pilot candidate please give us: expected average tokens per request, peak RPS, acceptable p99 latency, and whether they can tolerate batching. That lets us recommend Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

[03:58] Marcus Avery: Noted. NovaCare: 750 tokens avg, RPS low but spikes during claims window, p99 target 250 ms. Orion Retail: short prompts, high concurrency, p99 target 120 ms. Aegis Logistics: streaming, need under 100 ms ideally. BlueCrest: cannot use public multi-tenant for compliance.

[04:26] Lena Cho: A question — for dedicated reserved, how fast is autoscale and burst? Our reps will get pushback if capacity is slow.

[04:34] Jordan Blake: Good point. Dedicated can be configured with burst pools; autoscale has a configurable policy — typical ramp is seconds to minutes depending on warm workers, but we'll put exact SLA expectations in the doc. We'll also include fallback model variants for graceful degradation.

[04:51] Marcus Avery: Another thing — for execs they want to see joint references. Do you have any other healthcare references you can showcase where Redwood was co-sold through a partner?

[04:59] Jordan Blake: We have a couple of mid-market healthcare wins through partners — I'll check with CSMs and share anonymized case notes. Probably safe to say 'regional payer' references available.

[05:10] Priya Nair (Polaris): Thinking tactically: which two deals should we select as pilots? Criteria: compliance fit, near-term close probability, and technical feasibility.

[05:20] Jordan Blake: My read — pick one compliance-heavy (NovaCare or BlueCrest) and one fast-time-to-value high-concurrency (Orion or Aegis). That shows breadth. Thoughts?

[05:30] Marcus Avery: Agree, NovaCare plus Orion is a good combo. NovaCare buys trust, Orion buys velocity.

[05:36] Lena Cho: I like NovaCare and Aegis actually — Aegis is easier for engineering to stand up and demos well. But Orion has a clear buyer.

[05:44] Jordan Blake: Let's put NovaCare as primary pilot and Aegis as secondary, but Polaris to confirm champions for both. Lena, can you send the champion names by 12/22?

[05:54] Lena Cho: Yes, I'll send champions.

[06:00] Priya Raman: On benchmarks: for NovaCare we'll need private or VPC. If they require BAA and KMS, hosted multi-tenant may be out. We should scope out a Private deployment cost estimate.

[06:12] Marcus Avery: BlueCrest asked about air-gapped options — is that in roadmap?

[06:17] Jordan Blake: We have an on-prem package option for enterprise but it's more of an engaged SOW. For pilot, VPC + KMS usually suffices. We'll attach a note that air-gapped option exists but with longer lead time.

[06:30] [08:10] -- brief side chatter about holiday schedules, hiring freezes, and who will be out in early Jan --

[08:12] Miguel Santos: Back to co-sell plays — we should define a joint logo motion for the top pilot. That includes a joint press/email, exec brief, and a discrete pipeline credit for Polaris. Also double-check any conflict with Polaris channel agreements.

[08:29] Lena Cho: How about a 60-90 day pilot plan? Week 0-2 discovery, week 2-4 benchmark + technical proof, week 4-6 success criteria validation and pilot closure. That ties nicely to our sales cadence before freeze.

[08:44] Jordan Blake: Good. Priya, can you draft a benchmark checklist template so everyone collects the same telemetry?

[08:50] Priya Raman: Yup. Checklist will include request traces, token counts, p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hits if applicable, and error rates. Also include a basic QA prompt set for quality regression checks.

[09:03] Marcus Avery: On the sales tools — Polaris needs an easy one-pager on when to propose Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted so reps don't under- or over-sell.

[09:12] Jordan Blake: We'll create a decision tree: low-latency/high-concurrency -> Dedicated; compliance/KMS/BAA -> Private; short pilots or uncertain volume -> Hosted promo. We'll add recommended pricing buckets.

[09:24] Lena Cho: Can we also get a copy of your security artifacts? They asked for SOC2 cert and a data processing addendum.

[09:31] Jordan Blake: Yes — we'll share SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and the DPA template. Miguel will attach the vendor security pack.

[09:40] Marcus Avery: Competitor question — clients asked us if Redwood will lock them in given model variants and quantization choices. Any notes we can give to reassure them?

[09:50] Priya Raman: We recommend multi-model strategy, and we provide tools to export model outputs and checkpoints. For quant, there's a compatibility layer — not perfect but migration paths are documented. We can provide a short tech note.

[10:02] Lena Cho: Nice. On pricing again — what's the threshold for reserved capacity? If Polaris wants to bring in a mid-sized customer, what's the commitment?

[10:10] Miguel Santos: Typical reserved capacity starts around a few hundred thousand USD annual commit, but we can craft pilot-friendly reserved trials for strategic partners. We'll include hypothetical numbers in the spreadsheet.

[10:22] Jordan Blake: Let's go quick through the six deals and add a status + recommended play for each.

[10:28] Marcus Avery: NovaCare — high compliance, recommend Private/VPC, Pilot Probability: 60%.

[10:34] Jordan Blake: Orion Retail — high concurrency, recommend Dedicated or Hosted with warm workers, Pilot Prob: 45%.

[10:40] Marcus Avery: BlueCrest Fintech — Private, need SOW, Pilot Prob: 30%.

[10:45] Marcus Avery: Aegis Logistics — Hosted with streaming optimization or Dedicated, Pilot Prob: 55%.

[10:52] Marcus Avery: ISV pilot — smaller revenue, internal product pilot — low lift, Pilot Prob: 70%.

[10:58] Marcus Avery: Internal product team pilot — internal champion, Pilot Prob: 80%.

[11:06] Jordan Blake: OK. For the two pilots we agreed: NovaCare primary, Aegis secondary (pending champions). We'll schedule the benchmark for NovaCare as VPC test and Aegis on hosted demo.

[11:15] Lena Cho: We'll need the benchmark template and a kickoff deck for NovaCare.

[11:20] Jordan Blake: Miguel will share deck and pipeline spreadsheet.

[11:24] Priya Nair: A quick legal/procurement question — do you require a PO for pilots or can we do trial credits and then invoice?

[11:32] Miguel Santos: For small pilots under $15k we can do trial credits/virtual invoice. For pilots that require reserved capacity or on-prem packages we'll need a PO and SOW. We'll put thresholds in the playbook.

[11:45] Marcus Avery: Any blockers we foresee? For NovaCare it's procurement and legal on BAA and key management. For Aegis it's network access for streaming.

[11:55] Priya Raman: We'll do a short network diagram and onboarding doc to speed Aegis setup.

[12:02] Jordan Blake: Alright, next steps recap — Jordan: share joint pipeline sheet + playbook (due 12/21). Priya: benchmark checklist and technical notes (due 12/23). Miguel: security pack and margin one-pager + set up Slack channel (due 12/20). Lena: champions list and intro emails (due 12/22).

[12:20] Lena Cho: Sounds good. One last thing — can we plan a customer-facing joint webinar in Q1? Maybe "Operationalizing LLMs for Retail & Logistics" — Polaris can host.

[12:31] Jordan Blake: I like that. We'll add as an aspirational Q1 marketing item.

[12:36] Marcus Avery: Closing: thanks everyone. We'll expect the materials and aim to kick pilots before end of Jan ramp.

[12:45] Jordan Blake: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and calendar invites.

[12:52] -- meeting ended --
